extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians preparing and submitting manuscripts to the Journal of the American Mathematical Society (JAMS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting research articles to the Journal of the American Mathematical Society, including scope, peer-review process, submission format, required metadata, and post-acceptance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal of the American Mathematical Society (JAMS) is devoted to research articles of the highest quality in all areas of mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be research articles of the highest quality and within the broad remit of mathematics; editors may screen out material not suitable for the journal's subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles appearing in this journal are peer reviewed by external reviewers; JAMS uses a single-anonymous peer-review process in which reviewers know the authors but authors do not know the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors manage review; expectation is external peer review for articles that pass initial editorial screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial desk rejection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may reject papers without external review that are not suitable for publication in the journal due to reasons such as subject matter or clear weaknesses in scientific content or presentation style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subject suitability, sound scientific content, and adequate presentation/formatting to avoid immediate rejection without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred method of submission is to upload a PDF file using the Initial Manuscript Submission form (Centralized Manuscript Processing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use the Centralized Manuscript Processing system for initial submissions; an alternate method (sending one paper copy) is available but less preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata (paper copy alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper copy is being forwarded to the AMS, the following information is required with the submission: Name of the journal, Name of the corresponding author, Contact information including email address and mailing address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contact information, particularly email addresses, must be supplied to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest an appropriate Editor
rubrics_metrics.description: The author should suggest an appropriate Editor to review the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including a suggested editor helps with initial handling; choose an editor with relevant subject expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior publication / no simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper that has been previously published, or is being considered for publication elsewhere, should be submitted to the American Mathematical Society, nor may a paper that is under consideration by the American Mathematical Society be submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the manuscript is original and not under consideration at any other journal at time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Included with the footnotes to the paper should be the 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification representing the primary and secondary subjects of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MSC codes in the paper footnotes to indicate primary and secondary subject areas; use the 2020 MSC scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement (post-acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although an abstract is not required upon initial submission, upon acceptance authors will be requested to supply an abstract for the electronic version of this journal. An abstract should be at least one complete sentence and at most 300 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an abstract between 1 sentence and 300 words for the accepted paper; note that no abstracts appear in the printed journal starting in 1998, but electronic abstracts are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AMS style files and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use AMS-prepared style files in preparing their papers; the AMS Author Resource Center provides TeX resources and AMS journal article templates from Overleaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AMS style files/templates to conform to formatting expectations and reduce production issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must submit the Consent to Publish. All authors must agree regarding the Copyright Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required post-acceptance paperwork; failure to submit consent/copyright agreements will block publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access license selection for AMS Open Access journals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the article is to be published in one of the AMS Open Access journals, authors must agree which Creative Commons License will be selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide and record the appropriate Creative Commons license for OA publication as part of the post-acceptance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints / electronic PDF delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints are provided free of charge in electronic form to all authors. A downloadable and printable PDF version of each article is available from the AMS website following print publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will receive electronic offprints; ensure contact information is correct to receive notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions and reprinting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual readers and nonprofit libraries may make fair use (e.g., copy an article for teaching or research). Republication, systematic copying, or multiple reproduction is permitted only under license from the AMS; requests for permission are handled by the Copyright Clearance Center. Material for which the author holds copyright is excluded from AMS license permissions and must be requested from the author directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek permissions via the AMS/Copyright Clearance Center for reuse beyond fair use; check author-held copyright notices on articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing graphics and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The page links to resources including 'Preparing graphics' and 'Joint Author Guidelines for Preparing Accessible Mathematics Content'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AMS guidance for preparing figures/graphics and for making mathematics content accessible to ensure production-quality images and accessibility compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language editing and author resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Language editing services are available (e.g., from Charlesworth Author Services) and the AMS Author Resource Center provides additional tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors with language concerns or formatting questions are encouraged to use available editing services and AMS resources to improve clarity and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription and access notices (archiving policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: A current active subscription is required to view article PDFs in volumes published within the last five years; full article PDFs older than five years are freely available. The journal is indexed in major databases and archived in Portico and CLOCKSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand access restrictions and archiving; this is informational rather than a submission requirement but affects readership and access.
